Definition: from G1537 and G2556; to be (bad or) weak, i.e. (by implication) to fail (in heart):--faint, be weary.
BiblicalUsage: This word means to lose heart, to faint and be weary, and the Greek text spells it with a g sound, to fail, where Strong's lists it with a k. Jesus tells the parable of the unjust judge so that men ought always to pray and not to faint, and Paul says not to be weary in well doing, for in due season we shall reap if we faint not. The spelling differs, but the warning is the same.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe weariness is the enemy of prayer, because Jesus told His parable precisely so that we would pray on and not faint.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
